newsitem.title: USA: Conoco south Texas deal fuels growth plans.
newsitem.headline: Conoco south Texas deal fuels growth plans.

text.p: Conoco Inc expects ramped-up natural gas production from its newly acquired Lobo Trend acreage in south Texas to account for 20 percent of its worldwide oil and natural gas production by the year 2000 Executive Vice President Rob McKee said on Friday.

The $1.1 billion acquisition of the former TransTexas Gas Corp natural gas reserves was expected to more than double the company's current 800 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of North American production in five years, he said.

"We intend to take the production in the total Lobo area from about 250 (mmcfd) up to about 800 (mmcfd) over the coming five years. It's actually closer to 900 (mmcfd) by the time we get this five-year program in place," McKee said.
He said a fraction of the gas is already contracted for, but most will be marketed on the spot market.
"Basically, we'll go out and find buyers just like we do on the rest of our gas production, basically on an every day, every week, every month kind of basis," he said.

Conoco, a unit of Du Pont Co, said it planned to spend $1 billion over the next five years to develop the more than 2.7 trillion cubic feet of proved and estimated natural gas reserves acquired in the deal.
The reserves in the Lobo trend are relatively long-lived, with an estimated reserve-to-production life of 30 years compared to Conoco's current nine-year average, McKee said.
Conoco plans to drill 100 south Texas wells this year and 180 next year to exploit the newly acquired reserves, he said.
"We're trying to grow Conoco very aggressively in upstream...and the only way we can grow our business particularly is to grow the production that we have," he said.
